findings.message: The supplied bounded material contains validated candidates sourced only from comments comm_001692_제347조_Ⅳ.6_69 and comm_001692_제347조_Ⅳ.6_72, but the target declares eight additional comments as part of its source scope. Those additional comments were not supplied to this stage and cannot support this card set.
findings.recommended_action: Limit source_scope.comment_ids to the comments represented in the supplied validated candidates.

findings.message: The review questions introduce disputes about property-loss theories, triangular fraud, disposition authority, and credit-card issuance that are not present in the supplied candidate batch. They therefore imply unresolved norms and authority choices outside this stage's bounded source material.
findings.recommended_action: Remove the out-of-scope questions or retain only questions directly arising from the four supplied candidates.

findings.message: Several asserted coverage gaps concern triangular fraud, credit-card issuance, statutory amendment history, and precedent indexing not established by the supplied bounded material. A stage cannot characterize absent topics or external source coverage based on material it did not receive.
findings.recommended_action: Restrict coverage_gaps to limitations demonstrable from the supplied candidates, such as the lack of primary precedent text for the commentary-reported holdings.

findings.message: The note affirmatively directs a distinction between fraud-law benefit and a calculable Special Act gain, but this card's supporting passage states only that fraud-law property benefit need not be computationally quantifiable and that omission of its value is not unlawful. The asserted distinction is not stated in that source.
findings.recommended_action: Rephrase the note as a question requiring separate authority, or remove the unsupported Special Act distinction.

summary: The four cards substantially preserve the supplied candidates and their reported authority types, but the card-set metadata imports source scope, coverage gaps, and review disputes from material outside the bounded candidate batch. Those scope defects require revision; one card also contains an unsupported review-note distinction.
